::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--technical}
Technical Manual
:::

## What this workflow does

The mortality workflow turns authorised mortality REDCap records into an approved public mortality data package. It is separate from the CVD event workflow.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Workflow at a glance"}
1. Extract private mortality data.
2. Classify each death using the fixed CVD death-classification rules.
3. Calculate private counts, distributions and annual rates.
4. Apply disclosure control and review the proposed public files.
5. Approve the exact reviewed files.
6. Publish only the approved files.
:::

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    A["1. Extract mortality data"] --> B["2. Classify CVD deaths"]
    B --> C["3. Build mortality burden data"]
    C --> D["4. Apply controls and review"]
    D --> E["5. Approve reviewed files"]
    E --> F["6. Publish approved files"]
```

Each box is a separate controlled stage. Each arrow is a controlled move to the next stage. Completing a calculation is not approval, and approval is not publication.

## Run the workflow

| Stage | What it produces |
|---|---|
| [Step 1: Extract mortality data](extract.qmd) | A private death-certificate extract through a completed month. |
| [Step 2: Classify CVD deaths](classify.qmd) | A private classified mortality dataset and review summaries. |
| [Step 3: Build mortality burden data](build-burden.qmd) | Exact private counts, distributions and annual rates in a data-package folder. |
| [Step 4: Review the mortality data package](review.qmd) | Disclosure-controlled proposed public files and a private review workbook. |
| [Step 5: Approve the reviewed data package](approve.qmd) | An approval record and the exact private files authorised for publication. |
| [Step 6: Publish approved mortality outputs](publish.qmd) | The official public analytical package and its website copy. |

Steps 1–5 remain private. Step 6 is the only stage that copies approved analytical files into the public area.

## What the workflow prepares

The public mortality data package contains:

- mortality counts (`MORT-BURDEN-001`);
- annual percentage distributions (`MORT-BURDEN-002`);
- annual crude and directly age-standardised mortality rates (`MORT-RATE-001`), with their supplied 95% confidence intervals;
- Primary and Inclusive mortality definitions;
- monthly, quarterly and annual rows within the approved publication scope; and
- the fixed, reviewed 2015–2019 monthly historical reference.

The **Primary** definition includes Clear and Likely CVD deaths. The broader **Inclusive** definition also includes Possible CVD deaths. Some generated files use `upper_clear_likely_possible` for the Inclusive definition. Here, *upper* means the broader classification definition; it is not an upper confidence limit or an upper estimate from record linkage.

Disease case ascertainment officer (DCO) linkage is in the CVD event workflow, not this mortality workflow.

## Publication boundary

Step 6 copies the approved files to the official public analytical folder:

`$BNR_PUBLIC/metrics/mortality/burden/`

It also refreshes the website copy under:

`$BNR_REPO/site/downloads/files/metrics/mortality/burden/`

This analytical publication does not deploy the website. The Downloads catalogue must then be rebuilt, the site rendered and checked locally, and the approved website changes deployed through GitHub.

## Fixed workflow rules

- Positive supporting counts from 1 to 5 receive primary protection; zero is not automatically protected.
- The workflow applies any additional protection needed to stop a protected count being calculated from published totals.
- Reviewers check generated proposed files; they do not edit generated protection decisions or public files.
- Approval does not publish the data package.
- Generated datasets, supporting information, file lists and approval records are never repaired by hand.
